Definition: from G2121; to have good time, i.e. opportunity or leisure:--have leisure (convenient time), spend time.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, eukairéō is the word for have leisure (convenient time), spend time. In Mark 6:31, the text says "and they had no leisure so much as to eat." In Acts 17:21, the text says "For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that eukairéō matters because time belongs to God, and He keeps His appointments, even the long ones. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
